Foundation deployment and limited Firestore/WSS smoke checks are parent-verified; no actual consent/login, chat, raid or visual/OBS validation is claimed.

## How we used Codex

Codex authored all source, tests, documentation and the original SVG in this same thread. The initial sandbox blocker was repaired by the operator; work resumed here. The second increment added mocked OAuth, encrypted storage, bot methods and a Firestore adapter tested through injection, with its initial SDK installation failure reported honestly at the time. Parent review subsequently supplied installed dependencies; this thread generated the offline lockfile, verified the SDK import, updated committed streamer consent and reran all tests. The Must milestone then added the shared marks reducer, atomic quota/moderation integration, self-forget handling, deterministic original SVG runes and mocked regression tests. Parent review corrected the quota to five marks per viewer per stream and replaced the global forgetting hold with content erasure plus minimal bounded anti-abuse records. Curated `.codex-evidence/run-NNN.jsonl` and `.codex-evidence/SESSION_ID` are permitted; raw backups, other evidence, auth files, secrets and local env remain ignored. No raw backup or credential contents were read, no server was left running, and no commit was created. See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

### Should #3 — Chronicle (unpublished branch; off by default)

Atlas and stop pages now show one handwritten mythic fiction line per completed stop. It is a literary metaphor, not a factual journey claim or a personal mark attribution. No OAuth scopes changed: Keepers still need `channel:bot channel:manage:raids`; the bot still needs `user:read:chat user:write:chat user:bot`.

Optional **Write Chronicle for latest received stop** is an explicit private owner control POST, protected by the existing account-scoped session, exact Origin and CSRF checks. Only the stop recipient may attempt it. No generation occurs on startup, webhook acknowledgement, Atlas GET or search. The default `CHRONICLE_ENABLED=false` and `CHRONICLE_ALLOW_PAID=false` keep it off; absence of a key also keeps it off. The owner has said it will remain off. Templates need no key.

Paid generation would require prior owner approval, both gates set to `true`, and an owner-bound `OPENAI_API_KEY` Secret Manager environment reference (never a value in source, examples, logs or browser configuration). Even a small model can incur charges; no current price is asserted. The fixed model is `gpt-4.1-mini`, with 96 output tokens and one attempt per completed stop. Only the completed ring index and a fixed literary instruction leave the app: never marks, identities, account names or tokens. Generated plain text must be at most 160 Unicode characters and pass output moderation using `omni-moderation-latest` at `/v1/moderations` (the free moderation endpoint). Moderation errors, flagged/malformed output, URLs/HTML, empty output, timeouts and upstream errors use the template. No paid request retries occur.
